questions.question: What does a machine learning model actually learn?
questions.explanation: The model learns numerical weights (parameters) that define how inputs are transformed into predictions.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the loss function?

options.B: To measure how far predictions are from actuals

questions.explanation: Loss (e.g., MSE) quantifies mistakes — smaller loss means better predictions.

questions.question: Why is gradient descent more efficient than manual 'up/down/same'?

options.C: It uses gradients (direction & slope) to reduce error

questions.explanation: Gradients give the direction and steepness for fastest decrease in loss.

questions.question: What does the learning rate (α) control?
questions.explanation: α controls the step size: too big overshoots, too small is slow.

questions.question: In backpropagation, the chain rule is used to:

options.B: Compute each parameter’s contribution to total error

questions.explanation: Chain rule lets us trace how each parameter affects the final loss.
